label: Text
name: The Islamic Qur'an & Hadith Corpus
summary:
The Islamic Qur'an & Hadith Corpus comprises the two primary textual foundations of Islam: the Qur'an (the Word of God as revealed to the Prophet Muhammad through the angel Jibril between 610 and 632 CE) and the canonical hadith collections (reports of the Prophet's words, actions, and tacit approvals compiled in the 9th century CE). The Qur'an — 114 suras (chapters) arranged roughly by decreasing length — is considered by Muslims to be the literal, uncreated speech of God in Arabic, and is the most memorized book in human history (millions of huffaz worldwide).

The Six Canonical Hadith Collections (Kutub al-Sittah) — particularly Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim — form the basis of Islamic law (Shari'a), theology, and daily practice for 1.8+ billion Muslims worldwide. Together, these texts constitute the most widely studied and practiced textual tradition on Earth by population.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Islamic Qur'an & Hadith Corpus has shaped Islamic law, theology, and daily practice for over 1.8 billion Muslims worldwide, influencing global politics, culture, and society.
